title: License Key Formatting
summary: Given a license key represented as a string s that includes alphanumeric characters and dashes, and an integer k, reformat the string such that each group contains exactly k characters, except for the first group which may be shorter but must contain at least one character.
statement: Given a license key represented as a string s that includes alphanumeric characters and dashes, and an integer k, reformat the string such that each group contains exactly k characters, except for the first group which may be shorter but must contain at least one character. Additionally, convert all lowercase letters to uppercase and insert a dash between two groups. Return the reformatted license key.
constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 100,000; English letters, digits, and dashes only; 1 <= k <= 10,000.
Remove existing dashes, uppercase letters, then group from the right in groups of k. Only the first group may be shorter.
Return an empty string if the input contains only dashes. Never add a leading or trailing separator.
hints: Old dash positions do not constrain the new groups.
After cleaning, the first group length is total%k, or k if divisible.
Emit that first group, then full groups of k joined by a single dash.
Handle an all-dash input before creating the first group; uppercase letters without changing digits or order.
editorial: Only the first group may be short, so its length is determined by the cleaned length modulo k. All remaining groups are full-sized. The oracle independently slices backward from the right end and reverses the group order, covering partial first groups and empty cleaned inputs.

tests.explanation: Ignoring old dashes gives 5F3Z2E9W; split into two groups of four: 5F3Z-2E9W.
Five characters require a one-character first group: 2-5G-3J, not 25-G3-J.
